mcqs.question: Which of the following describes the correct way to use a ruler to measure the length of an object?

options.A: Place the ruler's zero mark at the object's left end and read the measurement at the right end.
options.B: Align the ruler's end with the object's right end and read from the left.
options.C: Hold the ruler at any point and estimate the length.
options.D: Place the ruler upside down and read the numbers.

mcqs.answer: Place the ruler's zero mark at the object's left end and read the measurement at the right end.
mcqs.explanation: The zero mark of the ruler must be aligned with the starting point of the object; the measurement is then read at the far edge. Option A follows this procedure. Options B, C, and D are incorrect because they either misalign the zero mark or do not use the ruler properly, leading to inaccurate measurements.

mcqs.question: Why is it important to align the zero mark of a ruler with the starting point of the object being measured?

options.A: To include the extra length of the ruler's edge in the measurement
options.B: To avoid adding an extra centimeter to the measurement
options.C: Because the zero mark is only decorative
options.D: It does not affect the measurement at all

mcqs.answer: To avoid adding an extra centimeter to the measurement
mcqs.explanation: If the zero mark is not aligned with the object's start, the measurement will include the distance from the ruler's edge to the zero mark, typically adding an extra unit (e.g., 1 cm). Aligning the zero mark prevents this error. Options A and C are false, and D contradicts the need for accuracy.

mcqs.question: When reading a metric ruler, which part of the scale gives the exact measurement of an object?

options.B: The line that aligns with the far edge of the object
options.C: The line that passes through the zero mark
options.D: The line that is farthest from the zero mark

mcqs.answer: The line that aligns with the far edge of the object
mcqs.explanation: The measurement is taken at the point where the object's far end meets the scale. The nearest whole number line may be an approximation, while the zero line is the starting reference, not the measurement point. Option B correctly identifies the reading point.

mcqs.question: A pencil lies between the 12 cm and 13 cm marks on a ruler and appears to be three‑quarters of the way from 12 cm to 13 cm. What is the best estimated length of the pencil?
mcqs.explanation: Three‑quarters of a centimetre is 0.75 cm. Adding this to the lower mark (12 cm) gives 12 cm + 0.75 cm = 12.75 cm. Options A and B underestimate, while D ignores the fractional part.

mcqs.question: A student measures a book’s length while looking at the ruler from an angle, causing a parallax error. Which action will most effectively eliminate this error?

options.A: Keep the eye directly above the ruler while reading the scale
options.B: Use a longer ruler to cover the whole book
options.C: Measure the book twice and take the average
options.D: Place the book on a tilted surface to see the scale better

mcqs.answer: Keep the eye directly above the ruler while reading the scale
mcqs.explanation: Parallax error occurs when the eye is not aligned with the scale, causing the reading to appear shifted. Viewing the ruler straight on (eye directly above) removes the error. Using a longer ruler or averaging does not address the viewing angle, and tilting the book worsens the problem.

mcqs.question: Which instrument should a student use to measure the length of a classroom rug that is about 3 meters long?
mcqs.explanation: A measuring tape can extend beyond 3 m and is flexible enough to lay along the rug, providing an accurate measurement. A 30 cm ruler and a meter stick are too short, and a micrometer is for very small dimensions.

mcqs.question: A student thinks the measurement should be taken from the far end of the ruler where the object ends, ignoring the zero mark. What is wrong with this method?

options.A: It gives a measurement that is too short
options.B: It gives a measurement that is too long
options.D: It only works for objects longer than the ruler

mcqs.answer: It gives a measurement that is too long
mcqs.explanation: By starting at a point other than the zero mark, the student adds the distance from the ruler’s edge to the zero mark, typically 1 cm, making the recorded length larger than the actual length. Option A is opposite, C is false, and D is irrelevant.

mcqs.question: If a student aligns the 1 cm mark of the ruler with the object's starting point instead of the zero mark, how will the recorded measurement compare to the actual length?

options.A: It will be 1 cm less than the actual length
options.B: It will be 1 cm more than the actual length
options.C: It will be the same as the actual length
options.D: It will be double the actual length

mcqs.answer: It will be 1 cm less than the actual length
mcqs.explanation: Starting measurement at the 1 cm mark skips the first centimetre of the object, so the reading omits that length, resulting in a value 1 cm shorter than the true length. Options B, C, and D do not reflect this omission.
